title: Restriction fibrations for diagrams with cocartesian marked edges
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, quasicategories, coherent functor simplicial sets and full subcategories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], categorical fibrations (inner fibrations lifting equivalence edges with specified source) of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], and cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $r:E\to P$ be a categorical fibration of quasicategories. Let $K$ be a small simplicial set, let $A\subseteq K$ be a simplicial subset, and let $f:K\to P$ be a simplicial map. Mark a set $M\subseteq K_1$ containing all degenerate edges, and give $A$ the inherited marking $M_A=M\cap A_1$.

Define $\operatorname{Lift}_f(K,E)$ in simplicial degree $d$ to consist of maps $H:K\times\Delta^d\to E$ with $rH=f\operatorname{pr}_K$, with operators given by restriction. Let $\operatorname{Lift}^{M}_f(K,E)$ be its full subcategory on those vertices $H:K\to E$ for which every edge of $M$ has $r$-cocartesian image. Use the same construction on $A$ and $f|_A$.

Both marked lift categories are quasicategories, and restriction is a categorical fibration
$$\operatorname{Lift}^{M}_f(K,E)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Lift}^{M_A}_{f|_A}(A,E).$$
The marked lift category is closed under equivalence edges in the unmarked lift category: if $H$ is a marked lift and $H\simeq H'$ over the identity of $f$, then $H'$ is a marked lift. All transformations and higher simplices in the displayed categories remain over the identity of $f$ or $f|_A$. No cocartesian lifts of other base arrows, operadic Segal conditions, approximation hypothesis, or existence of a marked lift is assumed.

proof.text: For $J=K$ or $A$, put $X_J=\operatorname{Fun}(J,E)$, $Y_J=\operatorname{Fun}(J,P)$ and $L_J=\operatorname{Lift}_{f|_J}(J,E)$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] to $\varnothing\subseteq J$: $p_J:X_J\to Y_J$ is a categorical fibration between quasicategories. Degreewise, $L_J=X_J\times_{Y_J}\{f|_J\}$. An inner horn in $L_J$ fills by lifting against $p_J$ over the constant simplex at $f|_J$; hence $L_J$ is a quasicategory. We will also need the following direct check: an edge of $L_J$ which is an equivalence in $X_J$ is an equivalence in $L_J$. Indeed every initial outer horn in $L_J$ whose initial edge is this edge fills over the constant simplex by [lem-cbc-inner-fibration-equivalence-outer-horn-lift]; the converse outer-horn criterion of [lem-cbc-equivalence-outer-horn-filling] applies inside the quasicategory $L_J$.

source.place: 01F1, empty-subset case; 01H0 and its opposite, followed by the converse equivalence outer-horn criterion

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] to $A\subseteq K$ and $r$, obtaining the categorical fibration $q:X_K\to T=X_A\times_{Y_A}Y_K$. The map $L_A\to T$ sends $h$ to $(h,f)$; its pullback of $q$ is exactly restriction $\rho:L_K\to L_A$, in every degree. Inner horns for $\rho$ fill using $q$ with this prescribed bottom simplex. For an equivalence $u:h\to h'$ of $L_A$ and $H\in L_K$ restricting to $h$, the image $(u,1_f)$ is an equivalence of $T$: its inverse and inverse-triangle witnesses are the images of those for $u$. Lift it through $q$ to an equivalence $H\to H'$ in $X_K$. The equation with $q$ puts this edge, including its endpoint, in $L_K$, and step 1 makes it an equivalence there. Thus $\rho$ is a categorical fibration with the specified-source convention.

source.place: 01F1, corner map and its explicit pullback to the fixed base diagram

proof.text: Let $\eta:H\to H'$ be an equivalence in $L_K$. The inclusion into $X_K$ preserves its inverse-triangle witnesses, so [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] makes each component $\eta_x:H(x)\to H'(x)$ an equivalence in $E$. Each $\eta_x$ is $r$-cocartesian: for every $n\geq2$ and initial outer horn with initial edge $\eta_x$ over a specified simplex of $P$, [lem-cbc-inner-fibration-equivalence-outer-horn-lift] supplies a filler. This is precisely the horn definition in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], applied to the inner fibration $r$.

source.place: 01DK and initial-horn dual of 01H0; the cocartesian horn definition

proof.text: Suppose $H$ is marked. Fix $m:x\to y$ in $M$. Restrict $\eta:K\times\Delta^1\to E$ to $m\times\Delta^1$. Its two standard triangles have a common diagonal $d:H(x)\to H'(y)$, with edge pairs $(H(m),\eta_y)$ and $(\eta_x,H'(m))$, respectively. The first triangle and [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] show $d$ cocartesian, since $H(m)$ and $\eta_y$ are cocartesian. In the second triangle $\eta_x$ is cocartesian, so the same node's cancellation clause implies that $H'(m)$ is cocartesian. This holds for each $m$, proving that the marked vertices are closed under equivalences in $L_K$. The argument with $K$ replaced by $A$ proves the corresponding assertion for $L_A$. It uses only the stated inner fibration and the given edges.

source.place: HTT Proposition 2.4.1.7, opposite-category composition and cancellation, applied twice to the naturality square

proof.text: The full simplicial subsets $L_K^M\subseteq L_K$ and $L_A^{M_A}\subseteq L_A$ are quasicategories: fill an inner horn in the ambient quasicategory; all its vertices are already vertices of the horn, hence are marked, so the filler lies in the full subset by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Restricting a marked vertex along $A\subseteq K$ preserves the required condition because $M_A=M\cap A_1$. Thus $\rho$ restricts to the displayed map of full marked subcategories.

source.place: Agent expansion: inner horns retain their vertices; inherited marking

proof.text: For an inner-horn lifting problem for $L_K^M\to L_A^{M_A}$, step 2 supplies a filler in $L_K$. Every vertex is already in the given horn, so fullness puts that filler in $L_K^M$. For an equivalence in $L_A^{M_A}$ with prescribed source lift $H\in L_K^M$, step 2 lifts its image in $L_A$ to an equivalence $H\to H'$ in $L_K$. Step 4 makes $H'$ marked. The lifted edge and its inverse-triangle witnesses have only the vertices $H,H'$, so fullness puts them in $L_K^M$. This proves the categorical equivalence-lifting condition. All fillers were constructed in the degreewise fibers $L_J$, and taking full subsets retains their simplices unchanged; consequently every transformation and higher simplex still lies over the identity of $f|_J$.

source.place: Agent expansion: restriction to full subsets using the closure proved in step 4

proof_origin.place: 01F1 supplies the unmarked corner fibration. The strict-fiber check and marked restriction are agent expansions using the cited existing horn, pointwise-equivalence and cocartesian-composition nodes; sources read online, not archived in literature/.

lean.statement: theorem inert_marked_restriction_fibration {K E P : SSet.{u}} (r : E ⟶ P) (hr : IsIsofibration r) (A : K.Subcomplex) (f : K ⟶ P) (M : Set (K _⦋1⦌)) (hM : ∀ x : K _⦋0⦌, K.σ 0 x ∈ M) : IsIsofibration (markedSectionRestriction r f M A) ∧ (∀ e : (sectionCategory r f) _⦋1⦌, IsEquivalenceEdge (sectionCategory r f) e → IsMarkedSection r f M ((sectionCategory r f).δ 1 e) → IsMarkedSection r f M ((sectionCategory r f).δ 0 e))
lean.note: Reuses the existing strict fixed-base sectionCategory and sectionRestriction. The three helpers impose only the specified cocartesian marking on vertices and restrict along the actual inclusion; there are no additional existence or operadic hypotheses. IsIsofibration includes both quasicategory conditions and prescribed-source equivalence lifting. Maintainer review extracts the marked restriction well-definedness obligation as a named sorry theorem, with its proof plan, retaining the same canonical map data and main signature.
